decision: A fork that is a whole redesign becomes a named layout inside its format; a brand pack picks it by name (formats.<f>.layout) and supplies values, never code
why: IU thumbnail v3 and the IU social scene graph are new designs, not recolours; lifting them as layouts keeps exact parity for every brand while the engine (parser, paths, pool, Chrome, CLI, contract) is shared

decision: Keep two banner designs, strip-centre (OBA) and strip-corner (IU), both brand-neutral, instead of one merged template
why: each fork's PNG and SVG already drift apart (IU glow 0.34 in the PNG vs 0.30 in the SVG; the OBA SVG ignores brand text colours), so a byte-parity merge would encode those quirks as fake brand values; brand-neutral designs give the real win: a new brand picks a design in one file

decision: Golden runs see the shared photo pool: a scratch fork is given the pool files it lacks, and the report names the ones its cases used
why: zoom-banner's Sep 17 headshots were deleted from its working tree, so the fork drew a monogram where Stencil drew the photo; no two pools hold different bytes under one name, so supplying only fills gaps

decision: Shared fix: a hidden PACE plate is display:none in the corner design
why: the IU template left the hidden img laid out in the header row; unreachable for IU (CE line required) but it would shift any brand without PACE

decision: VET banner SVG now takes VET's own muted text, line and pill colours, matching its PNG; logo layer named VBI
why: the OBA SVG twin hard-coded OBA's colours while the PNG used VET's; no real VET banner input exists, so there is no parity case to hold
